doc.title: Artie Shaw — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Tommy Dorsey the mensch; rounded versus one-dimensional musicians; Bill Evans
summary: Tommy was more of a whole person than Goodman, and Shaw contrasts single-focus players with rounded ones like Bill Evans and Gil Evans.

story.theme_name: Playing with Coltrane and the avant-garde

blocks.x: Now Tommy [Dorsey] was not like that. Tommy played like he was.
More of a rough and tumble guy.
Yeah. He had a big temper. He broke a lot of trombones.
More of a person. Yeah. A mensch, as we say.
There are one or two musicians that you hear of who are superb players, but there doesn’t seem to be much else outside the musician.

It’s unfortunate, as I say. See a guy like Bill Evans, I think was a great player, and he seemed to have a view of the world. Bill was a rounded person. Unfortunately the junk [heroin] did him in. Gil Evans was another guy who knew something about the world.
